paper_title: Early-Universe Simulations of the Cosmological Axion
coupling_convention: m_a in eV (x-axis), f_a in GeV (y-axis)
notes: This paper presents early-universe numerical simulations of axion dark matter in the post-inflation PQ symmetry breaking scenario. The primary result is a determination of the axion mass that produces the observed dark matter density: m_a = 25.2 ± 11.0 μeV, corresponding to f_a = (2.27 ± 0.33) × 10^11 GeV. This is a cosmological/theoretical constraint on the axion mass-decay-constant plane, not an experimental exclusion limit. The paper uses high-resolution lattice simulations starting before the PQ phase transition and evolving through the QCD phase transition to matter-radiation equality. The uncertainty includes statistical errors from simulation variance across different λ̃ values, systematic uncertainties from scaling violations (~15%), fixed g_* assumption (~10%), and uncertainties in axion mass growth (~27%). The result is presented as a single point (or narrow band) on the f_a-m_a plane rather than a traditional exclusion curve. The paper also discusses minihalo mass functions and implications for axion detection experiments like HAYSTAC, but the primary new constraint is the m_a determination. This is NOT an experimental exclusion limit but rather a theoretical prediction from first-principles simulations of early-universe axion cosmology. | Auto-corrected couplings: ×1e-16 (×1.00e-16, rule=argmin|log10(median*f)-log10(anchor=3.2e-05)|)
